head: 153,862 people in 92 countries read together for 12 hours.
summary: Guinness World Records has confirmed that 153,862 people in 92 countries read at the same time during a 12-hour session on 8 October, a new mark for the most people reading online in 12 hours. The National Literacy Trust and the British Council ran the Take 10 to Read challenge, with more than 3,000 schools, libraries, families and hobby groups joining authors online for ten minutes of quiet reading; outside the United Kingdom the biggest groups logged on from Romania, India and Pakistan, and readers also took part from the Cayman Islands, Afghanistan and Venezuela. The adjudicator Will Munford presented the certificate at Malmesbury Primary School in east London on 4 November alongside the children's author Rashmi Sirdeshpande, and a second went to Holy Child Senior Secondary School in New Delhi.

head: A Dumfriesshire village raised £45,000 and bought its own church.
summary: Friends of Wamphray Church has completed the purchase of the 1834 kirk in the hills south of Moffat from the Church of Scotland, after raising more than £45,000 in under a year. Donations came from across the United Kingdom and from supporters in the United States and Canada, topped up by a £12,500 grant from Clyde Windfarm and SSE Renewables; the chair, Carol Beattie, said the group was grateful for the time it was given to raise the money and build support. Secretary Rob Harrison says the first job is plumbing in toilets, with a condition survey to follow, and the building opens again for a Remembrance service on Sunday and the village carol service on Christmas Eve.

head: People from 79 nations planted 2,500 trees together in one Hessen forest.
summary: Six hundred and eighty-five people from 79 countries planted 1,750 sessile oaks and 750 hornbeams in the Eulerwald on the edge of Dietzenbach, south-east of Frankfurt, on 24 October. The non-profit Waldfreunde gGmbH ran the day with more than 20 volunteers and a HessenForst forester, Benedikt Reiss, who showed newcomers how to set a sapling; everyone brought a passport so the Rekord-Institut für Deutschland could count nationalities, and its adjudicator Meike Janz handed over the certificate the same day. The previous mark of 66 nationalities had stood since a planting in Qatar, and the organisers chose the date because it falls on United Nations Day.

head: Nearly 250 volunteers spent the All Saints' weekend collecting for Warsaw's oldest gravestones.
summary: Nearly 250 volunteers — actors, musicians and journalists among them — carried collection tins along the paths of Warsaw's Stare Powązki cemetery from 9am until about 8pm on 31 October and 1 November, in the 52nd year of the appeal. The Jerzy Waldorff committee that runs it took about 270,000 złoty last year, money that went toward conserving 27 historic monuments alongside 1.9 million złoty in city grants. Forty more gravestones are booked for restoration next year, out of roughly 300 the committee still counts as urgent and about 1,700 saved over five decades.

head: Nine combines turned up to bring in a neighbor's 400 acres of soybeans.
summary: Nine combines, about six grain semis and six tractors with grain carts converged on a soybean field near Walton, Illinois, on October 19 to bring in the roughly 400 acres Michael Mead could not harvest himself after a medical emergency in July. Neighboring farmer Don Meyer made the calls and got so many offers that he started a waiting list; Prairie State Tractor Repair sent a technician to keep the machines running, and the Southwest Taco Truck drove out from Amboy with lunch. Meyer is holding that list for Mead's corn harvest, a return of the ten days Mead once spent helping clean up Meyer's own farm.

head: Over 600 volunteers spent four days rebuilding Pacific Palisades together.
summary: Over 600 volunteers spent four days this week repairing homes, building children's playhouses, and restoring shared spaces across Pacific Palisades, California, nine months after a January fire destroyed thousands of houses there. Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles organized the push, working with the Foothill Catalog Foundation and the City of Los Angeles, which pre-approved dozens of house designs to speed permits for returning families. The group plans to keep returning in waves as more families secure permits, turning what had been a slow, solitary rebuilding process into a shared one.
